source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 12 'Individual Retirement Accounts', Withdrawals, item 1; PDF page 14 IMPORTANT (retired before 59 1/2: cost recovery until 59 1/2); PDF page 8 'INCOME NOT TAXABLE FOR PA PIT PURPOSES' first bullet; the PA-40 has no Social Security line; PDF page 15 Line 3

worked: Required minimum distribution at 75 is an IRA distribution after 59 1/2; Social Security is out in full. Federal AGI = IRA distribution person 0 40,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 + dividends 10,000.00 = 75,500.00. Taxable Social Security is the federal worksheet's result on the gross benefit and other income. Federal taxable income = 75,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 + age 65 addition 2,000.00 = 57,750.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 75,500.00; less 40,000.00 IRA distribution person 0 (born 1950-09-09, 59 1/2 on 2010-03-09) (pa_ira_from_59_5); less 25,500.00 taxable Social Security (social_security exempt; gross 30,000.00; no PA line); income after reliefs = 10,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 10,000.00. Tax = 10,000.00 x 0.0307 = 307.00. No credit in the projection; state income tax 307.00. Form: Line 1a/1c 0.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 10,000.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 10,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 10,000.00; Line 12 307.00. Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 10,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
